title: Failure-class retry policy for online requests
description: Add a failure-class retry policy for online request processing. Create a new pure module `src/bespokelabs/curator/request_processor/online/retry_policy.py` (standard library only — `dataclasses`, `enum`, `typing`; it must not import `aiohttp`, `time` or `random`) containing: `class FailureClass(str, enum.Enum)` with exactly the members `THROTTLE = "throttle"`, `TRANSIENT = "transient"`, `CONTRACT = "contract"`, `TERMINAL = "terminal"` in that declaration order; `classify_failure(exc: BaseException) -> FailureClass`, which never raises and consults four signals, returning on the first that matches — (1) an `int` HTTP status read from `getattr(exc, "status_code", None)` falling back to `getattr(exc, "status", None)`, matched against `400 -> CONTRACT`, `401/403/404 -> TERMINAL`, `408/409/425 -> TRANSIENT`, `413/422 -> CONTRACT`, `429/529 -> THROTTLE`, with any other status in 500-599 mapping to `TRANSIENT` and any other `int` (or non-`int`) falling through to the next signal; (2) the exception type, matched by `__name__` walked along `type(exc).__mro__` in order against `TimeoutError/ConnectionError/ClientConnectorError -> TRANSIENT`, `ValueError/ValidationError/JSONDecodeError/KeyError -> CONTRACT`, `PermissionError/NotImplementedError -> TERMINAL`; (3) substrings of `str(exc).lower()`, scanned in table order — `"rate limit"`, `"ratelimit"`, `"too many requests"`, `"overloaded"`, `"quota"` -> `THROTTLE`; `"timed out"`, `"timeout"`, `"connection reset"`, `"temporarily unavailable"`, `"response is empty"` -> `TRANSIENT`; `"invalid api key"`, `"authentication"`, `"permission denied"` -> `TERMINAL`; (4) a `TRANSIENT` default. Also define `@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True) class RetryVerdict` carrying `should_retry`, `failure_class`, `attempt_index` (1-based index of the attempt that just failed), `delay_seconds` (`>= 0.0`, and `0.0` whenever `should_retry` is False), `attempts_left_after`, `tracker_field` (the name of the single `OnlineStatusTracker` counter this failure belongs to: `THROTTLE -> "num_rate_limit_errors"`, `TRANSIENT`/`TERMINAL` -> `"num_api_errors"`, `CONTRACT -> "num_other_errors"`) and `reason_code` (`f"{failure_class.value}:{outcome}"`, where `outcome` is one of `"retry"`, `"exhausted"`, `"abort"`); `class RetryPolicy` with `__init__(self, clock: t.Callable[[], float], jitter: t.Callable[[], float]) -> None` (both injected, neither defaulted), `delay_for(failure_class: FailureClass, attempt_index: int) -> float` giving the exponential-backoff wait for that class and attempt, `decide(exc: BaseException, *, attempts_made: int, attempts_left: int, ...) -> RetryVerdict` which classifies the exception and prices it against the request's remaining retry budget without mutating anything, and `apply_to_tracker(tracker: t.Any, verdict: RetryVerdict) -> None`, which increments exactly the counter named by `verdict.tracker_field` and, for throttle verdicts only, stamps `tracker.time_of_last_rate_limit_error` and extends (but does not shorten) `tracker.throttle_cooldown_until` — a new `OnlineStatusTracker` dataclass field, `throttle_cooldown_until: float = 0.0`, placed immediately after `time_of_last_rate_limit_error`; `remaining_cooldown_seconds(tracker: t.Any, now: float) -> float` returning `max(0.0, round(tracker.throttle_cooldown_until - now, 3))`; `format_failure_summary(failure_log: t.Sequence[tuple[FailureClass, str]]) -> list[str]`, one `f"[{failure_class.value}] {message} (x{count})"` entry per distinct `(class, message)` pair, sorted by count descending with ties broken by first occurrence in the log, `[]` for an empty log; and `format_attempt_label(attempts_made: int, max_retries: int) -> str` returning `f"attempt #{attempts_made + 1} of {max_retries + 1}"`. `APIRequest` gains `attempts_made: int = 0` and `failure_log: list = field(default_factory=list)` (appended after the existing fields, `attempts_left` keeps its name and its seeding from `config.max_retries`); `BaseOnlineRequestProcessor.__init__` builds `self.retry_policy`; the `except Exception as e:` block in `handle_single_request_with_retries` is rewritten to call `decide` then `apply_to_tracker`, append `(verdict.failure_class, str(e))` to `request.failure_log`, write the verdict's budget values back onto the request, and — when `should_retry` — log the class and `reason_code`, set `request.retry_not_before` from the verdict delay and re-queue, otherwise emit the usual `GenericResponse` with `response_errors=format_failure_summary(request.failure_log)`. `cool_down_if_rate_limit_error` is rebuilt on `remaining_cooldown_seconds`, the retry loop's attempt log uses `format_attempt_label`, and the hand-rolled rate-limit blocks in the openai/anthropic/litellm processors stop mutating tracker counters (their compensating `num_api_errors -= 1` / `num_other_errors -= 1` lines are deleted) while still raising.

requirement.rule: `decide` sets `attempt_index = attempts_made + 1` and then prices the failure in attempts, with per-class costs that are not all 1: `TRANSIENT` costs 1, `CONTRACT` costs 2, and `THROTTLE` costs 0 for as long as the request still holds a throttle waiver. The waiver budget is a third piece of per-request state that `decide` takes and returns: `retry_policy` exports `DEFAULT_THROTTLE_WAIVERS: int = 6`, `APIRequest` gains `throttle_waivers_left: int = DEFAULT_THROTTLE_WAIVERS`, `decide`'s full keyword signature is `decide(exc, *, attempts_made: int, attempts_left: int, throttle_waivers_left: int)`, and `RetryVerdict` has an eighth field `throttle_waivers_after: int` sitting between `attempts_left_after` and `tracker_field` (field order: `should_retry`, `failure_class`, `attempt_index`, `delay_seconds`, `attempts_left_after`, `throttle_waivers_after`, `tracker_field`, `reason_code`). On a `THROTTLE` failure with `throttle_waivers_left > 0` the cost is 0 and `throttle_waivers_after = throttle_waivers_left - 1`; once the waivers are spent the cost is 1 and `throttle_waivers_after` stays 0. Every other class leaves `throttle_waivers_after == throttle_waivers_left`.
requirement.scope: The waiver counter is per-request state carried on `APIRequest` and seeded at construction from `DEFAULT_THROTTLE_WAIVERS`; it is not a config knob, not a field on `OnlineStatusTracker`, and not shared across requests. `decide` stays pure — it reads the three budget numbers handed to it and returns the new ones on the verdict; the base-class `except` block is what assigns `request.attempts_made = verdict.attempt_index`, `request.attempts_left = verdict.attempts_left_after` and `request.throttle_waivers_left = verdict.throttle_waivers_after`.
requirement.exclusions_or_crossover: `TERMINAL` is never retried and discards the rest of the budget: `should_retry=False`, `attempts_left_after=0` even when `attempts_left` was 7, `throttle_waivers_after` untouched, outcome `"abort"`. Conversely a zero-cost `THROTTLE` at `attempts_left == 0` satisfies `0 - 0 >= 0` and is still retried (`"throttle:retry"`, `attempts_left_after == 0`) — a spent budget only stops a throttle failure once the waivers are also gone.
requirement.failure_behavior: Exhaustion is decided after the cost is subtracted, not before: if `attempts_left - cost < 0` the verdict is `should_retry=False`, `attempts_left_after=0` (clamped, never negative), `delay_seconds=0.0`, outcome `"exhausted"`. So a `CONTRACT` failure at `attempts_left == 1` is exhausted rather than being granted a last try that leaves the budget at `-1`.
requirement.observability: With a jitter source returning 0.25: `decide(Exception("rate limit"), attempts_made=0, attempts_left=3, throttle_waivers_left=6)` yields `(should_retry, attempt_index, attempts_left_after, throttle_waivers_after) == (True, 1, 3, 5)`; `decide(Exception("rate limit"), attempts_made=9, attempts_left=0, throttle_waivers_left=3)` yields `should_retry is True`, `attempts_left_after == 0`, `throttle_waivers_after == 2`, `reason_code == "throttle:retry"`, while the same call with `throttle_waivers_left=0` yields `reason_code == "throttle:exhausted"`; `decide(ValueError("bad"), attempts_made=0, attempts_left=3, throttle_waivers_left=6)` gives `attempts_left_after == 1`, and at `attempts_left=1` gives `(False, 0, "contract:exhausted")`; `decide(Exception("invalid api key"), attempts_made=2, attempts_left=7, throttle_waivers_left=6)` gives `(False, FailureClass.TERMINAL, 3, 0.0, 0, 6, "num_api_errors", "terminal:abort")`. `DEFAULT_THROTTLE_WAIVERS == 6` and a freshly built `APIRequest` reports `throttle_waivers_left == 6`, `attempts_made == 0`, `failure_log == []`.

fragmentation_sources: chat thread in the curator engineering channel arguing that a 429 says nothing about the request and should not burn its budget, ending with someone capping the free passes

incident write-up email about a run where a provider outage returned 429 for twenty minutes and requests looped until the run was killed — the source of the cap and of the 'terminal zeroes the budget' line
wiki page on structured-output failures that records the double charge for schema violations and the 'subtract then check' ordering
reply in a mail thread noting that the exhausted branch must clamp at zero because the number is printed in the final status line
hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: An earlier build made throttle failures free with no cap at all (rate limits simply never decremented `attempts_left`), which the outage postmortem reversed in favour of a bounded six-waiver allowance per request.

requirement.rule: `delay_for(failure_class, attempt_index)` reads `(base, factor, cap)` from a per-class schedule — `THROTTLE (8.0, 2.0, 60.0)`, `TRANSIENT (0.5, 3.0, 20.0)`, `CONTRACT (0.0, 1.0, 0.0)`, `TERMINAL (0.0, 1.0, 0.0)` — computes `raw = min(cap, base * factor ** (attempt_index - 1))` so the cap is applied *before* jitter and the result can never exceed `cap`, returns `0.0` at once when `raw <= 0`, and otherwise returns `round(raw * (0.5 + 0.5 * j), 3)`, where `j` is the value from the injected jitter source clamped into `[0.0, 1.0]` by `min(1.0, max(0.0, j))`. This is half-jitter, not full jitter: the delay is always in `[raw/2, raw]`. None of these numbers come from `config.seconds_to_pause_on_rate_limit`, which becomes dead configuration that the policy never reads.
requirement.scope: The jitter source is consumed exactly once per positive delay and not at all otherwise: `RetryPolicy.__init__` calls neither callable, `delay_for` invokes `jitter()` only on the `raw > 0` path, and `decide` calls `delay_for` only when it is about to return `should_retry=True` — an aborted or exhausted verdict sets `delay_seconds = 0.0` without consulting the schedule. `clock` is likewise untouched by `delay_for` and `decide`; it is called once, and only for `THROTTLE` verdicts, inside `apply_to_tracker`.
requirement.exclusions_or_crossover: `CONTRACT` is retried but never waits: a `CONTRACT` verdict carries `delay_seconds == 0.0` and consumes no jitter draw, exactly as `TERMINAL` does, so re-asking after a schema violation is immediate while a `TRANSIENT` failure at the same attempt index waits. `TRANSIENT` also uses factor 3.0 rather than the 2.0 that `THROTTLE` uses.
requirement.failure_behavior: `delay_for` raises `ValueError` when `attempt_index < 1` (attempt indices are 1-based); it does not silently treat 0 or a negative index as the first attempt, and it does not draw jitter before validating.
requirement.observability: With a jitter source returning 0.25 (multiplier 0.625): `delay_for(THROTTLE, 1) == 5.0`, `(…, 2) == 10.0`, `(…, 3) == 20.0`, `(…, 4) == 37.5` and `(…, 9) == 37.5`; `delay_for(TRANSIENT, 1) == 0.312`, `(…, 2) == 0.938`, `(…, 3) == 2.812`, `(…, 4) == 8.438`, `(…, 5) == 12.5`, `(…, 20) == 12.5`; `delay_for(CONTRACT, 1) == 0.0` and `delay_for(TERMINAL, 3) == 0.0`. With jitter 0.0 `delay_for(THROTTLE, 1) == 4.0`; with 1.0, `8.0`; with the out-of-range 2.5, `8.0`; with `-1.0`, `4.0`. `delay_for(THROTTLE, 0)` raises `ValueError`. Counting calls into the jitter source: three `decide` calls on `ValueError("bad")` with a healthy budget leave the count at 0, one `decide` on `Exception("rate limit")` raises it by exactly 1, an exhausted `TimeoutError` decision leaves it unchanged, and constructing a `RetryPolicy` leaves it at 0.

hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: The first cut reused the existing `seconds_to_pause_on_rate_limit` (10.0) as a single base for every class with plain doubling and full jitter; it was reversed after a run's tail sat in multi-minute uncapped sleeps and the config knob was left in place purely for backwards compatibility.

brief:
Retry policy for online requests: what a failed request costs before it is tried
again, and how a caller can tell which failures were which.

The area, concretely:
- `src/bespokelabs/curator/request_processor/online/base_online_request_processor.py` —
  the `APIRequest` dataclass (line 43, `attempts_left`), seeded from
  `config.max_retries` at line 374; `handle_single_request_with_retries()`
  (line 474) whose `except Exception as e:` block (lines 526-563) increments
  `num_other_errors` (line 527) for every failure alike, decrements
  `attempts_left` (line 537) and re-queues with `retry_queue.put_nowait(request)`
  (line 543) — immediately, with no delay of any kind; and the permanent-failure
  path (lines 545-563), which collapses the accumulated errors with `Counter`
  into `f"{error}(x{count})"`.
- `cool_down_if_rate_limit_error()` (line 298) — a flat, global
  `seconds_to_pause_on_rate_limit` sleep computed off
  `status_tracker.time_of_last_rate_limit_error`, awaited before every request
  in both the main loop (line 388) and the retry loop (line 436).
- The three places a rate-limit error is actually recognised, all of them in
  provider subclasses and none in the base:
  `openai_online_request_processor.py` lines 299-300,
  `anthropic_online_request_processor.py` lines 285-286,
  `litellm_online_request_processor.py` lines 429-430 — each stamping
  `time_of_last_rate_limit_error` and `num_rate_limit_errors` on the tracker.
- `status_tracker/online_status_tracker.py` — `num_rate_limit_errors` (line 56),
  `num_api_errors`, `num_other_errors`, `time_of_last_rate_limit_error`
  (line 67), and the error line those three feed (lines 148-150).
- `request_processor/config.py` — `max_retries` (line 28, default 10, `ge=0`)
  and `seconds_to_pause_on_rate_limit` (line 111, default 10, `gt=0`), the only
  two retry knobs that exist.

Three mechanisms disagree about what a retry costs, and the disagreement is
reachable. The retry queue says zero: every exception is re-queued at once. The
cooldown says a flat global pause, applied to requests that were never rate
limited. The config says one number for all error kinds. Classification lives in
three provider subclasses, so the base class cannot tell a 429 from a schema
violation and charges them the same. The attempt number is computed from the
same expression at two moments — line 424 before the attempt, line 540 after the
decrement — and both are printed. Read all of it and design the fix as one fully
specified retry policy: a classifier, a delay schedule, and one decision object
the queue, the log and the tracker all read.

Constraints: pure and deterministic, no network, no sleeping, no threads. Both
the clock and the source of jitter are injected, never read from `time` or the
`random` module inside the policy. The design must be testable by calling the
classifier and the schedule directly on exception instances and attempt numbers,
and by driving the retry decision with a fake tracker — no aiohttp session, no
event loop, no provider.
